themes.name: Can post-Chicago economic theories justify changing the traditional legal tests for monopoly power and exclusionary conduct?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether newer theories of strategic conduct, entry barriers, and market power warrant replacing or modifying established antitrust doctrine.

members.name: Can post-Chicago economic theories justify changing the traditional legal tests for monopoly power and exclusionary conduct?

themes.name: Can nonprice conduct by technology and Internet firms constitute monopolization or attempted monopolization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether conduct involving data, access, interoperability, user engagement, information, or platform design can establish competitive harm without an immediate price increase.

members.name: Can nonprice conduct by technology and Internet firms constitute monopolization or attempted monopolization?

themes.name: Can monopoly leveraging occur when a firm uses power in one market or transaction to obtain advantages in another?
themes.definition: This question tests competing economic views about whether power in one domain can be profitably extended through contractual, organizational, or strategic conduct elsewhere.

members.name: Can monopoly leveraging occur when a firm uses power in one market or transaction to obtain advantages in another?

themes.name: Can mergers and interfirm collaboration promote innovation while also entrenching market power?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how antitrust should balance innovation incentives and productive cooperation against the risk that consolidation or collaboration suppresses future competition.

members.name: Can mergers and interfirm collaboration promote innovation while also entrenching market power?

themes.name: Can merger review reliably predict non-price effects on innovation, quality, and market development?
themes.definition: This question investigates the evidentiary and analytical methods needed to assess merger effects that are not captured by conventional price-and-output measures.

members.name: Can merger review reliably predict non-price effects on innovation, quality, and market development?

themes.name: Can merger law address threats from acquisitions of nascent or potential competitors more effectively than monopolization law?
themes.definition: This question examines whether Section 7 merger enforcement is the appropriate tool for preventing incumbent acquisitions that may eliminate future competition when present market effects are difficult to prove.

members.name: Can merger law address threats from acquisitions of nascent or potential competitors more effectively than monopolization law?

themes.name: Can merger enforcement mistakenly reduce consumer welfare by blocking efficient combinations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the risk that intervention against concentrated business combinations will eliminate cost savings, competitiveness, innovation, or other benefits of integration.

members.name: Can merger enforcement mistakenly reduce consumer welfare by blocking efficient combinations?

themes.name: Can market power exist or produce competitive harm despite low conventional market shares?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether barriers to entry, control of key inputs or platforms, network effects, or other conditions reveal power that market-share measures miss.

members.name: Can market power exist or produce competitive harm despite low conventional market shares?

themes.name: Can general antitrust law adequately regulate bottleneck facilities, vertical integration, and rival access without sector-specific obligations?
themes.definition: This question asks whether competition law alone can address exclusionary control over essential inputs, infrastructure, or distribution channels, or whether specialized access regulation is necessary.

members.name: Can general antitrust law adequately regulate bottleneck facilities, vertical integration, and rival access without sector-specific obligations?

themes.name: Can economically informed antitrust standards reduce both false positives and false negatives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether structured economic tests can distinguish harmful exclusion from vigorous competition without chilling beneficial business conduct or shielding anticompetitive practices.

members.name: Can economically informed antitrust standards reduce both false positives and false negatives?

themes.name: Can economic models of competitive markets reliably identify unlawful conduct in labor markets?
themes.definition: This question applies antitrust analysis to employer coordination and other labor-market practices while assessing whether conventional assumptions adequately capture worker harm and market power.

members.name: Can economic models of competitive markets reliably identify unlawful conduct in labor markets?

themes.name: Can economic efficiency reliably distinguish procompetitive conduct from unlawful exclusion by dominant firms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether efficiency claims and economic models can separate legitimate competitive superiority from conduct that forecloses rivals or harms competition.

members.name: Can economic efficiency reliably distinguish procompetitive conduct from unlawful exclusion by dominant firms?

themes.name: Can dominant technology platforms' market power be explained by scale and innovation, or does it primarily reflect anticompetitive conduct?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether economies of scale, network effects, innovation, and control over digital infrastructure justify platform dominance or conceal exclusionary behavior.

members.name: Can dominant technology platforms' market power be explained by scale and innovation, or does it primarily reflect anticompetitive conduct?

themes.name: Can digital platforms and technology-enabled markets harm competition without explicit collusion?
themes.definition: This question asks whether network effects, data advantages, algorithmic coordination, interoperability restrictions, and non-price harms require adaptations to conventional antitrust doctrine.

members.name: Can digital platforms and technology-enabled markets harm competition without explicit collusion?

themes.name: Can concentrated firms simultaneously overcharge consumers and underpay suppliers in ways that require antitrust intervention?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether antitrust should address coordinated or unilateral exercises of power that harm both downstream consumers and upstream suppliers.

members.name: Can concentrated firms simultaneously overcharge consumers and underpay suppliers in ways that require antitrust intervention?

themes.name: Can cartel leniency and private enforcement effectively deter secret horizontal agreements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether amnesty programs, private damages actions, and cooperation among enforcement institutions improve detection and deterrence of concealed cartel conduct.

members.name: Can cartel leniency and private enforcement effectively deter secret horizontal agreements?

themes.name: Can buyer-side market power be used to exclude rivals or deter entry even when consumers do not immediately face higher prices?
themes.definition: This question examines monopsony, strategic purchasing, and buyer concentration as mechanisms for restricting suppliers, competitors, or downstream market access.

members.name: Can buyer-side market power be used to exclude rivals or deter entry even when consumers do not immediately face higher prices?

themes.name: Can antitrust enforcement effectively address acquisitions and concentration after a transaction has closed?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal authority, practical effectiveness, and remedial limits of challenging consummated mergers or restructuring entrenched corporate power.

members.name: Can antitrust enforcement effectively address acquisitions and concentration after a transaction has closed?

themes.name: Can antitrust effectively address monopsony and buyer power at concentration levels below those associated with seller market power?
themes.definition: This question examines how labor-market, procurement, and other buyer-side restraints should be identified and distinguished from legitimate purchasing efficiency.

members.name: Can antitrust effectively address monopsony and buyer power at concentration levels below those associated with seller market power?

themes.name: Can antitrust courts and agencies reliably evaluate uncertain counterfactual competitive effects?
themes.definition: This question concerns the evidentiary and institutional difficulty of predicting what would have happened absent the challenged conduct, including the risk of both over- and under-enforcement.

members.name: Can antitrust courts and agencies reliably evaluate uncertain counterfactual competitive effects?

themes.name: Can anticipated entry reliably justify permitting substantial market concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether low entry barriers, prospective entrants, or alternative purchasers provide a sufficiently credible constraint on the power created by a merger.

members.name: Can anticipated entry reliably justify permitting substantial market concentration?

themes.name: Can agency enforcement policy legitimately change substantive antitrust doctrine without legislative revision?
themes.definition: This question examines how nonjudicial policymaking, FTC practice, enforcement priorities, and agency procedures influence the operational meaning of broad statutory standards.

members.name: Can agency enforcement policy legitimately change substantive antitrust doctrine without legislative revision?

themes.name: Are private antitrust litigation restrictions justified by the costs of meritless claims and excessive deterrence?
themes.definition: This question evaluates standing, purchaser classifications, recovery rules, litigation incentives, and the tradeoff between private enforcement and abusive or inefficient lawsuits.

members.name: Are private antitrust litigation restrictions justified by the costs of meritless claims and excessive deterrence?

themes.name: Are platform access restrictions efficient coordination or anticompetitive monopoly leveraging?
themes.definition: This question asks whether a platform's restrictions on interoperability, access, or participation protect product quality and innovation or instead extend monopoly power into adjacent markets.

members.name: Are platform access restrictions efficient coordination or anticompetitive monopoly leveraging?

themes.name: Are individual criminal penalties more effective than firm-level fines for deterring serious cartel conduct?
themes.definition: This question compares personal sanctions with corporate financial penalties in addressing secret coordination and aligning enforcement consequences with the incentives of responsible decision-makers.

members.name: Are individual criminal penalties more effective than firm-level fines for deterring serious cartel conduct?

themes.name: Are existing merger-review procedures and institutional arrangements adequate to identify harmful post-merger effects?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether merger guidelines, agency procedures, and institutional design effectively predict and remedy competitive harms that emerge after consolidation.

members.name: Are existing merger-review procedures and institutional arrangements adequate to identify harmful post-merger effects?

themes.name: Are existing antitrust doctrines adequate for platform self-preferencing and other forms of digital structural favoritism?
themes.definition: This question asks whether conventional exclusion and monopolization standards can identify anticompetitive conduct by platforms that favor their own products, services, or affiliated participants.

members.name: Are existing antitrust doctrines adequate for platform self-preferencing and other forms of digital structural favoritism?

themes.name: Are cartel sanctions and private remedies necessary and proportionate for deterring collusion?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the credibility of penalties, treble damages, and private litigation as deterrents while considering overdeterrence, strategic lawsuits, and compensation.

members.name: Are cartel sanctions and private remedies necessary and proportionate for deterring collusion?
